queries.text: How did American cities change across four decades (1980-2024): gentrification, inequality, affordability, and displacement — every claim cited?
Median household income growth rate in major US metros 1980 vs 2024
Gentrification index or share of neighborhoods classified as gentrified by Census tract from 1980 to 2010
Housing price appreciation percentage change for owner-occupied homes in US cities between 1980 and 2023
Rent burden ratio (rent-to-income) for renters in top 50 US metro areas in 1980 versus 2023
Poverty rate among residents living below the federal poverty line in selected US cities in 1980, 1990, 2000, and 2020
Income inequality Gini coefficient or ratio of median income in highest quintile to lowest quintile by city from 1979 to 2022
Displacement rate defined as share of households moving out due to rent increases or displacement events per year in gentrifying neighborhoods 1984-2016
Change in racial composition percentage point shift for Black and Hispanic populations in specific gentrified urban cores between decennial censuses 1980-2020

search_hits.title: Urban Gentrification Metrics: Four Decades of American City Transformation (the exemplar report)
search_hits.snippet: The operator's exemplar report (vendored as source-report.pdf): New York City leads with a Gini coefficient of 0.5469 versus the national average of 0.40 in 2013, while Atlanta and Miami follow at 0.57 and New Orleans at 0.56; the Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024 (+225% since January 2000); 48 of the 50 largest metros saw worsening mobility with Houston the sole improvement (+1.1%).
